title: Narrowing conversions, list initialization, and constexpr initializers
recap: Brace initialization rejects many narrowing conversions because they can lose information. Some constant-expression conversions are allowed when the compiler can prove the exact value is representable.
An explicit cast acknowledges a conversion but does not make an invalid value valid. Validate runtime values first, then convert the known-safe result.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice narrowing conversions, list initialization, and constexpr initializers.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement clampChannel(value), returning an unsigned char in [0,255]. Negative inputs become 0, inputs above 255 become 255, and in-range values are preserved. Do not allow wraparound. This challenge uses runtime range validation followed by an explicit narrowing conversion.
hints: Clamp using the int parameter before casting.
Do not cast a negative or too-large value and then try to fix it.
The return type is part of the function interface.
